newsitem.title: USA: Wall Street shares seen steady to higher at open.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street shares seen steady to higher at open.

text.p: Wall Street shares are expected to open steady to moderately higher Friday, buoyed by momentum from yesterday's late-session rebound but not immune to further profit-taking.
Stocks and bonds will take some early direction from durable goods data for June, due at 0830 EDT/1230 GMT.

"I expect we will move higher, given the positive momentum yesterday," said Alan Ackerman, market strategist at Fahnestock & Co. "But it will be a tug-of-war between those taking trading profits and those who want to increase positions."

The Dow industrials closed up 29 points at 8117 on Thursday, but not before a drop of nearly 100 points as investors took profits following exuberant gains sparked by Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's upbeat testimony to Congress on the U.S. economy.
While blue chips could consolidate some of their gains today, the market will likely wend its way higher as investors continue to buy on dips, analysts said.

"Barring a surprise in durable goods, the stock market will probably open steady and maybe move higher, because that's what it wants to do day after day," said Pierre Ellis, senior economist at Primark Decision Economics.
In early trading, the Standard & Poor's 500 futures index was off 1.50 points at 944.65. The long bond was flat at a yield of 6.44 percent.

Durable goods orders were expected to show a rise of 1.4 percent in June, compared with a decline of 0.7 percent in May. A strong rise in orders could temper some stock market enthusiasm, analysts said.
"Everyone is so at ease, believing the Fed will not tighten," Ellis said. "If, all of a sudden, the data show an indication of very strong demand, some of this complacency would be shaken a bit."
A muted durable goods number would further allay fears that the U.S. economy is overheating, Ackerman said.
The stock market will also find support from second quarter corporate earnings, which have been solid so far, analysts said.
The Wall Street Journal said in its Heard on the Street column that according to some analysts, the recent slide in Latin American phone stocks could create a buying opportunity.
The New York Times said in its Market Place column that Delta Air Lines Inc's focus on cost-cutting may have blurred the company's vision somewhat.
